text: ds-pstack 是面向 DeepSeek Harness 的多 agent 工程工作流插件。它向技能注册表发布随包提供的 playbook、原则与操作技能，并在 agent 请求阶段按委派任务分类，为子 agent 从用户勾选的模型池中选择模型和推理强度。分类采用确定性规则，不另发模型请求。用户可通过 /setup-pstack 选择推理预算并为角色固定路由；技能可从技能菜单调用，poteto-mode 将调查、开发、评审和验证等工作组织为步骤。适合希望在 Harness 中使用工程工作流并为不同子任务配置模型的开发者。使用前需在设置中勾选至少一个供子 agent 使用的模型。

ds-pstack adds engineering playbooks to DeepSeek Harness and routes delegated tasks to models from the checked subagent pool using deterministic classification. /setup-pstack sets reasoning budgets and role routes. A checked subagent model is required.
想让 DSH 根据子任务自动给委派的 agent 挑选合适模型。
我希望给不同工作类型的子 agent 设置推理预算和固定模型。
有没有能把工程开发流程、评审和验证步骤整理成可调用技能的工具？
让 DSH 按任务是编码、研究还是评审来调整子 agent 的模型。
I want delegated agents to get a model chosen for the kind of task they are doing.
How can I use structured engineering playbooks and principles as skills in DeepSeek Harness?
ds-pstack 的功能「任务路由」：读取子 agent 的委派任务并分类，再从设置中勾选的模型路由里选择模型和推理强度。子 agent 首次请求时触发。
ds-pstack 的功能「工程技能目录」：扫描随包的技能目录，将包含有效名称和描述的技能注册到 DSH 技能目录，供用户按需读取技能正文。
ds-pstack 的功能「预算与角色路由设置」：通过 /setup-pstack 记录推理预算及角色路由固定项，路由器读取该文件来调整路由选择。
ds-pstack 的功能「工作流 playbook」：poteto-mode 将开发请求匹配到调查、修复、功能开发等 playbook，并组织调用相关技能完成各步骤。
ds-pstack 使用前须知：路由器需要 DSH 设置中至少一个已勾选的子 agent 模型；候选池为空时会沿用当前路由。
希望减少手动挑模型，让系统按子任务类型和难度选择推理配置。
Can I publish reusable engineering playbooks as selectable skills in DSH?

| --- | --- | --- |

| 子 agent 模型 / Subagent model | 每个角色写死一个模型 slug / a model slug per role | 按任务意图从你勾选的模型池里自动挑 / routed by task intent from your checked pool |
| 分类开销 / Routing cost | n/a | 确定性规则分类，分类不调用模型 / deterministic classification, no model call |

@local/ds-pstack README · 快速安装 / Quick install：```
plugin_manager install_bundle github:monkeyin92/ds-pstack#main
```

然后 / then:

1. Settings → Subagent model selection，打开并勾选你想给子 agent 用的模型 / enable it and check the models you want
2. 运行 `/setup-pstack` 选预算 / pick a budget
3. 开干 / go:

```
/poteto-mode this pr has a subtle bug where the scroll drifts every 750ms even when idle. repro first, then fix and verify.
```

其他常用 / Other handy skills: `/interrogate` 对抗式 review，`/how` 讲清一个子系统，`/poteto-help` 不知道用哪个时问它。

---

@local/ds-pstack README · 快速安装 / Quick install：[pstack](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/tree/main/pstack) for DeepSeek Harness. pstack is Lauren Tan's set of agent workflows: write less code, but higher quality code, and parallelize with confidence.

This port keeps pstack's playbooks, principles, and prose rules. Two things change, because DeepSeek Harness works differently from Cursor.

@local/ds-pstack README · 快速安装 / Quick install：**The skills are the same skills.** All 58 of them, in the `/` menu under their pstack names. `/poteto-mode` runs the playbook, `/interrogate` runs the adversarial review, `/how` explains a subsystem, and the 24 `principle-*` skills carry the reasoning pstack is built on.

@local/ds-pstack README · 快速安装 / Quick install：**The models are chosen for you, out of your own list.** pstack on Cursor names a model slug per role. ds-pstack cannot do that, because a Harness profile's models are whatever you configured and checked. So the router reads the child's task, decides what kind of work it is, and picks the best route from the models you checked for subagents. A skill never names a model. The router picks from that checked pool, and `/setup-pstack` is the only place a route is pinned.

@local/ds-pstack README · Install：The package installs as a Harness bundle, straight from this repository:

```
plugin_manager install_bundle github:monkeyin92/ds-pstack#main
```

That adds two plugin rows to the profile. Disable either one to keep the other.

| Row | What it does when disabled |
| --- | --- |
| `ds-pstack-skills` | pstack's skills leave the catalog; routing still works |
| `ds-pstack-router` | every child runs on the route it inherited; skills still work |

@local/ds-pstack README · Updates：Installing from the repository means updates are a pull, not a reinstall. The profile records a git dependency, so the next fetch picks up whatever is on `main`:

```
dsh plugin --profile <profile> update @local/ds-pstack
```

@local/ds-pstack README · Updates：The profile's package manager resolves the branch to a commit and records both. Skill text reloads from disk on its own. The router's JavaScript is a separate module generation, so after an update that changes `lib/` the plugin has to be re-mounted: toggle the `ds-pstack-router` row off and on in Plugin Manager, which re-imports the module. A full app restart also works, and is the simpler option if you are unsure.

@local/ds-pstack README · Updates：To develop against a checkout instead of the published copy, install it by path (`plugin_manager install_bundle /absolute/path`) and reinstall from the git spec when you are done.

To stay on a fixed release instead of tracking `main`, install a tag:

```
plugin_manager install_bundle github:monkeyin92/ds-pstack#v0.1.0
```

A tag pins that commit until you install again. New tags are published as `v<version>` when the version in `package.json` changes.

@local/ds-pstack README · The model pool is yours：ds-pstack chooses only from the routes checked in **Settings → Subagent model selection** (`subagent-model-selection-settings.allowedModels`). That setting is the authorization boundary, so the router never widens it: the route it selects is always one you checked, even when another model would suit the task better.

@local/ds-pstack README · The model pool is yours：Checking one model means each routed child runs on that model with a routing-chosen effort. Checking several means the router can match a cheap fast model to mechanical work and a strong one to review. With none checked, the router leaves each child on the route it inherited. A forked child keeps its inherited route unless `routeForkedChildren` is turned on, and a delegation that already names `provider`, `model`, or `reasoning_effort` is left alone.
@local/ds-pstack README · The model pool is yours：To check models, open Settings, find Subagent model selection, enable it, and select the routes you want available.

section: How a child's route is chosen

text:
@local/ds-pstack README · How a child's route is chosen：The decision made from the child's own prompt is cached, so later requests from that subagent reuse it until the checked pool drops that route or the route fails. A guess borrowed from the parent task is not cached. The journal at `~/.dsh/ds-pstack-router.jsonl` records every decision and every skip.

Three rules bound the guess:
section: How a child's route is chosen
How a child's route is chosen

text: @local/ds-pstack README · Classification is deterministic：`scores` in the journal explain every decision. Phrase hints score the intent. The opening instruction outweighs later context, a hard or easy read can move the score, and ties go to the more specific reading: "rename the util file" is mechanical work, not a feature, even though it names a file. No model request is spent classifying, because a child should not wait on a judgement call before it starts. When every hint scores zero and the task is not marked hard or easy, the fallback intent is coding, and the child is still routed.

@local/ds-pstack README · Budgets：pstack's four budget labels still apply. `/setup-pstack` writes the one you choose:

| Budget | Base effort | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `unlimited` | `max` | everything thinks as hard as its route allows |
| `large` | `xhigh` | the router default |
| `medium` | `high` | cheaper, still thorough |
| `small` | `medium` | cheapest; mechanical work lands on `low` |

@local/ds-pstack README · Budgets：The intent shifts the base: planning, coding, debugging, research, and analysis start at the budget, review and writing sit one step below, and mechanical edits sit two steps below. A task that reads hard goes up one step, and an explicitly trivial one goes down one. The requested effort never goes below `low`, and it then snaps to an effort the chosen route advertises.

@local/ds-pstack README · Configuring roles：A pin wins over classification, which is what letting a human decide means. A pin whose route is no longer checked is treated as stale and ignored rather than sent, so unchecking a model also unpins it.

@local/ds-pstack README · Verification skills：`/create-verification-skill` and `/create-formal-verification-skill` generate project-local skills, so agents can prove a change works instead of asserting it. `/create-verification-skill` writes `.dsh/skills/verify-<app>/`, which Harness scans. `/create-formal-verification-skill` writes a project-local skill and does not name a directory. A project skill of the same name outranks ds-pstack's own.

@local/ds-pstack README · What did not port：Cursor-only machinery: Automations, the Bugbot feed, cloud agents, and `-fast` speed selection. Where a playbook step needs one, the skill says so in one line and continues. The full mapping is in [docs/harness/deepseek-harness.md](docs/harness/deepseek-harness.md).

@local/ds-pstack README · Upstream：pstack is MIT licensed by Lauren Tan. Its license is kept in [LICENSE.pstack](LICENSE.pstack), and the unmodified upstream README is in [README.pstack.md](README.pstack.md). Skill text is pstack's, adapted where a Cursor-specific name had to become a Harness one. Where a step needs Cursor-only machinery, the skill says so in one line and continues.

@local/ds-pstack README · Development：99 tests cover classification and its positional weighting, delegate-preamble stripping, path stripping, effort mapping, model ranking, pool enforcement, pin conflicts, fork protection, quarantine policy, privacy redaction, failure recovery, frontmatter parsing, and catalog publication. They run with no build step and no dependencies. The `skills/poteto-mode/scripts/` tooling has its own 73-test Bun suite, and `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs both plus `bun run typecheck` and `bash -n`.
